message.content:
We have
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+100=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\alpha+1)(\beta+1)=-99.
\]
Let
\[
a=\alpha+1,\qquad b=\beta+1.
\]
Then
\[
ab=-99
\]
and, since \(|\alpha|=|\beta|=M\),
\[
|a-1|=|b-1|=M.
\]

Because \(ab\neq 0\), we have \(a\neq 0\). Write
\[
a=x+iy,\qquad S=|a|^2=x^2+y^2>0.
\]
Since \(b=-99/a\), we have
\[
b=-\frac{99}{a}=-\frac{99\overline{a}}{S}.
\]

Let \(T=M^2\). First,
\[
T=|a-1|^2=|a|^2-2\operatorname{Re}(a)+1=S-2x+1,
\]
so
\[
x=\frac{S+1-T}{2}.
\]

On the other hand,
\[
T=|b-1|^2=\left|-\frac{99}{a}-1\right|^2
=\left|1+\frac{99}{a}\right|^2.
\]
Since \(1/a=\overline{a}/S\), this becomes
\[
T=\left|1+\frac{99\overline{a}}{S}\right|^2
=1+\frac{198x}{S}+\frac{9801}{S}.
\]
Substituting \(x=(S+1-T)/2\), we get
\[
T=1+\frac{99(S+1-T)}{S}+\frac{9801}{S}.
\]
Multiplying by \(S\),
\[
ST=100S+9900-99T.
\]
Thus
\[
T(S+99)=100(S+99).
\]
Since \(S>0\), we may divide by \(S+99\), yielding
\[
T=100.
\]
Therefore
\[
M^2=100,
\]
and since \(M\ge 0\),
\[
M=10.
\]

It remains to show this value is attainable. Take \(\alpha=10\) and \(\beta=-10\). Then
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+100=-100+10-10+100=0,
\]
and
\[
|\alpha|=|\beta|=10.
\]

Hence the only possible value is

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
